articles.title: Headmaster detained after BBC investigation into alleged sexual abuse of students
articles.description: Former students launched their own investigation, spending years collecting evidence and testimonies from others who say they were abused by the headteacher.

articles.title: Marcy Kaptur: longest-serving congresswoman’s bid for another House term roiled by anti-trans ad
articles.description:
Democrat in Congress since 1983 rebuked over ‘dangerous’ campaign ad – will it harm her chances in tight Ohio race?

Last month, Marcy Kaptur, the longest-serving woman in congressional history, released a video advertisement in which she looks directly at the camera and says exactly what she thinks about one of the most divisive issues facing Democrats today.

“Here’s the truth: I voted with Republicans to keep transgender ideology out of our schools because parents know what’s best for their kids,” Kaptur says, “and boys should not play in girls’ sports.”

Continue reading...

articles.title: UK savings: 5% interest rate deals may not last, say experts
articles.description:
Competition is hotting up, with National Savings & Investments lifting rates to the highest in years

National Savings and Investments (NS&I) has increased the returns on some of its accounts, with many now paying more than 5% for the first time in nearly three years.

Competition in the savings market has been growing, leading to some of the highest interest rates for years.

Continue reading...

articles.title: Flydubai co-pilot planned suicide attack on Israeli airport, UAE prosecutors say
articles.description:
Hammam al-Hammami is believed to have been targeting the passenger terminal at Ben Gurion airport near Tel Aviv

The co-pilot who tried to seize control of a passenger jet flying from Dubai to Tel Aviv last week was planning to launch a suicide attack targeting the passenger terminal at Israel’s international airport, prosecutors in the United Arab Emirates said on Friday.

Hammam al-Hammami attacked the plane’s Indian pilot with an emergency axe, but failed to prevent his badly injured colleague from opening the cockpit’s security door to allow passengers to overpower his assailant.

Continue reading...

articles.title: Two Latvians arrested at RAF base in Cambridgeshire released on bail
articles.description:
Men found inside RAF Molesworth, used by US and Nato for intelligence, freed on strict conditions as police continue investigation

Two Latvian men have been released on bail after being arrested at an RAF base in Cambridgeshire used by the US military and Nato.

The two men, aged 32 and 26, were arrested at 2am on Thursday after they were discovered inside RAF Molesworth in Cambridgeshire, which is used by the US military and Nato for intelligence operations.

Continue reading...

articles.title: Tory tax break for banks has cost UK public purse £6bn, says TUC
articles.description:
Exclusive: Chancellor urged to reverse Rishi Sunak’s tax surcharge cuts to claw back billions in lost revenue

  • Business live – latest updates

Tax cuts for big banks have deprived the UK government of £6bn in revenues, according to campaigners, who are calling on the chancellor, John Healey, to increase taxes and force lenders to pay their “fair share” in the upcoming budget.

Calculations by the Trades Union Congress (TUC), which represents unions with more than 5.3 million members across England and Wales, shows that the public purse is billions of pounds worse off as a result of tax cuts introduced under the Tory chancellor Rishi Sunak in 2023.

Continue reading...

articles.title: Firmus pulls biggest ASX float since Telstra amid investor doubt about datacentre company
articles.description:
The $11-a-share offer would have been the biggest debut on the stock market since the telecommunication giant in 1997

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

Firmus Technologies has scrapped what was set to be Australia’s biggest company listing in decades after investor demand for its much-hyped AI datacentre business failed to materialise.

A Firmus spokesperson said the board decided that proceeding with the offer was no longer in the best interests of the company and its shareholders.

Continue reading...

articles.title: Egyptian journalists plan weekend protest over detention of six colleagues
articles.description:
Matsadaash staff allege torture and forced confessions after being held on charges of working for Muslim Brotherhood

Egyptian journalists are planning a new protest in Cairo this weekend after six colleagues were charged with terrorism offences amid allegations they had been tortured in police detention.

Last week, Egyptian authorities arrested the journalists, from the independent factchecking and investigative platform Matsadaash, accusing them in a statement of being unlicensed and producing false news on behalf of the outlawed Muslim Brotherhood.

Continue reading...

articles.title: Thousands march in Madrid after death of evicted pensioner Maricarmen
articles.description:
Rally to remember woman, 87, whose rent battle with investment firm triggered nationwide protests over housing crisis

About 20,000 people took part in a march through the centre of Madrid on Thursday evening in memory of María del Carmen Abascal, the 87-year-old woman whose eviction from her flat in the capital a fortnight before her death triggered mass protests over Spain’s housing crisis.

The pensioner, whose flat had been bought by an investment firm that sought to increase her rent by 230%, had become the public face of the crisis before her death in hospital on Wednesday night.

articles.title: DoJ seeks to charge ex-Trump aide who gave key testimony on January 6 attack
articles.description:
Cassidy Hutchinson told panel she had been told Trump lunged for wheel of SUV to try to join mob at Capitol

Prosecutors in the justice department’s civil rights division are seeking criminal charges against Cassidy Hutchinson, a former top Trump White House aide who gave explosive testimony to the committee that investigated the US attack on the Capitol, according to a person familiar with the matter.

The potential charges involve lying to Congress, the person said.

Continue reading...

articles.title: Top bosses at Goldman Sachs to share bonus pot worth up to $500m
articles.description:
Eye-watering sum, to be split between 20 bankers, is one of the biggest payouts in the bank’s history

Top bosses at Goldman Sachs are in line to share a bonus pot worth up to $500m (£378m) this year, marking one of the biggest payouts in the Wall Street bank’s history.

The eye-watering sum will be shared between 20 bankers, with its chief executive, David Solomon, due to take about $100m (£75.6m) of the reward, which is made up of Goldman Sachs stock.

Continue reading...

articles.title: Two Latvian men arrested at RAF base in Cambridgeshire used by US military
articles.description:
Men aged 32 and 36 detained on suspicion of trespass, causing criminal damage and entering a prohibited place

Two Latvian men were arrested in the early hours of Thursday after they were discovered inside the perimeter of RAF Molesworth, a Cambridgeshire base used by the US military and Nato for intelligence operations.

The men, 32 and 36, were picked up at 2am inside the base, in an investigation that began four hours earlier when military police discovered an abandoned vehicle outside the facility.

Continue reading...

articles.title: Thousands to march in Madrid after death of evicted pensioner Maricarmen
articles.description:
Rally to remember woman, 87, whose rent battle with investment firm triggered nationwide protests over housing crisis

Thousands of people are expected to march through the centre of Madrid on Thursday evening in memory of María del Carmen Abascal, the 87-year-old woman whose eviction from her flat in the capital a fortnight before her death triggered mass protests over Spain’s housing crisis.

The pensioner, whose flat had been bought by an investment firm that sought to increase her rent by 230%, had become the public face of the crisis before her death in hospital on Wednesday night.

articles.title: Asos says customers’ names, contact details and search histories hacked
articles.description:
Experts say breadth of data accessed could help attackers devise “highly convincing” phishing scams

  • Business live – live updates

Asos hackers gained access to millions of customers’ recent search histories as well as names, addresses and phone numbers, the online fashion retailer has revealed.

Terms typed in by customers such as “glamorous wide fit” and “Asos petite” were in the data accessed in the cyber-attack, which emerged on Tuesday after app users received a notification titled “Asos hacked” with a link to the Telegram messaging service.

Continue reading...

articles.title: Search warrants used in Andrew Mountbatten-Windsor raids were unlawful, court rules
articles.description:
Judge makes ruling after former prince brought judicial review of operation linked to Jeffrey Epstein investigation

Andrew Mountbatten-Windsor has won his legal challenge against Thames Valley police over search warrants that led to his arrest.

The former prince brought a judicial review of the legality of the force’s actions and those of the central criminal court, which granted the warrants.

Continue reading...

articles.title: Tanker hit by multiple projectiles in Gulf off Qatar, maritime agency says
articles.description: Casualties have been reported on the vessel, identified by a maritime intelligence firm as the oil and chemical tanker, Acers.

articles.title: Teacher who sexually abused pupil back in Indonesia jail after BBC investigation
articles.description: Mochamad Subchi Azal Tsani had been secretly released on parole in 2025, after serving less than half his sentence.

articles.title: Residents airlifted to safety after flooding in central Chile
articles.description: The Mapocho river has burst its banks after an unusually large amount of rain fell in recent days.

articles.title: Oil prices jump 5% on Middle East tensions and US hurricane threat
articles.description:
Global bond market sell-off continues and stocks fall amid reports White House has asked to see options for more strikes against Iran

Oil prices have risen sharply amid fears about escalating tensions in the Middle East and a squeeze on production from the threat of a hurricane off the US coast.

Brent crude, the international benchmark, rose by 5% to $105.3 a barrel on Thursday, triggering a wave of selling in the global bond and stock markets.

Continue reading...

articles.title: Tesco lifts profit forecast and says consumer confidence is resilient
articles.description:
Sales rise 2% to £33.8bn in the past six months, helped by strong trade online

  • Business live – latest updates

Tesco has raised its annual profit forecast as the supermarket group said consumer confidence has remained relatively resilient this year despite ongoing geopolitical tensions “creating uncertainty”.

The UK’s biggest grocer said sales rose just 2% to £33.8bn in the first six months of its financial year but underlying profit was up 6.5% to £1.8bn.

Continue reading...

articles.title: South Korea threatens legal action if fuel shipments to Russia found to have broken law
articles.description:
Responding to a Guardian report that revealed thousands of tonnes of fuel was transported to Russia, Seoul said it was investigating the cases

South Korea will take legal action if it finds that shipments of fuel from its ports to Russia broke domestic law, the government has said, responding to a Guardian report on the trade.

The government, in a statement issued by the foreign and trade ministries and the customs service, said that it is “checking additional information concerning the loading cases reported by the Guardian” and “if the verification establishes that our laws and regulations have been violated, it plans to act in accordance with the law”.

Continue reading...

articles.title: Japan beer giants raided over suspicions they colluded to set the price of beverages
articles.description:
Investigators probe Asahi, Kirin, Suntory and Sapporo breweries – which together control more than 90% of Japan’s beer market

Japanese authorities have raided the country’s four biggest breweries over suspicions they colluded to set the price of beer and other beverages – a practice media reports said could have forced drinkers to pay over the odds.

Officials from the Fair Trade Commission this week searched the offices of Asahi Breweries, Kirin Brewery, Suntory Beer and Sapporo Breweries – which together control more than 90% of the domestic market. The quartet are suspected of violating the anti-monopoly law.

Continue reading...

articles.title: FBI says it thwarted terrorist attack in Minnesota by an 18-year-old it supplied with an AK-47
articles.description:
Authorities say they arrested an 18-year-old who was planning a shooting attack at the Mall of America

FBI officials stopped a potential terrorist attack on the Mall of America in Bloomington, Minnesota, authorities announced Wednesday. An 18-year-old was arrested on one count of obtaining a firearm to carry out an act of terrorism.

Sheikhdoon Abdullahi Mohamud had been investigated over the last nearly two years by the FBI. He was arrested Tuesday in a public park after he paid $600 to an undercover FBI employee posing as a member of the Islamic State for an AK-47 and 200 rounds of ammunition, according to the criminal complaint.

Continue reading...

articles.title: Christa Pike’s lawyers hold press conference after she regains consciousness in hospital – latest updates
articles.description:
Tennessee prisoner awake and speaking after surviving state’s attempt to execute her last Wednesday

  • Christa Pike is conscious and speaking after botched execution attempt, lawyers say

Tennessee’s top prison official is resigning following Christa Pike’s botched execution attempt.

Over the weekend, governor Bill Lee announced that Frank Strada, the department of correction commissioner, will leave his position in late October amid an independent investigation into Pike’s failed execution attempt.

Continue reading...

articles.title: Ex-Barclays traders jailed for rigging interest rates have convictions quashed
articles.description:
Acquittals of five former bankers come year after supreme court overturned ruling against City trader Tom Hayes

Five more former traders who were jailed for rigging interest rates have had their convictions quashed by the court of appeal in London, after a long battle to clear their names.

The court overturned the convictions of Jay Vijay Merchant, Jonathan Mathew, Philippe Moryoussef, Alex Pabon and Colin Bermingham – all of whom worked at Barclays.

Continue reading...

articles.title: Canada’s Weston family buys Boots for $8.9bn
articles.description:
Former Selfridges owners buys UK high street institution from long-term backer Stefano Pessina

The Canadian family that once owned Selfridges department store has bought UK pharmacy and beauty retailer Boots for $8.9bn (£6.74bn).

Wittington Investments, the holding company of the Weston family that controls the Loblaws grocery chain and Drugmart pharmacy chain in Canada, will own Boots’ UK and Irish retail operations and opticians chain, the No7 beauty brand and a franchise arm in Thailand.

Continue reading...

articles.title: British billionaire warned Epstein was a ‘sexual deviant’ decades before FBI closed in on the abuser
articles.description:
Sir James Goldsmith’s links to Hilton Head, South Carolina, add to mystery of Jane Doe 4, who claimed she was abused by Epstein in the 1980s

For Jeffrey Epstein, the billionaire Goldsmith family was a gateway to elite society and he wanted to be in their circle.

The disgraced financier, who died in prison in 2019 facing sex-trafficking charges, longed for a billionaire’s lifestyle and cultivated the family’s friends, bankers, business associates and advisers.

Continue reading...

articles.title: Shell refineries forecast to make double the profit from every barrel of fuel
articles.description:
Record prices caused by global shortages amid shutdown of war-damaged refineries in Middle East and Russia

Shell’s refineries are expected to make almost double the profit from every barrel of fuel produced owing to record prices caused by shortages around the world.

In a market trading update on Wednesday, the energy supermajor forecast profit margins of $42 a barrel in the July to September period, far above the $24 a barrel of the second quarter and the previous high of about $28 in mid-2022.

Continue reading...

articles.title: Police routinely failing to investigate ‘revenge porn’ in England and Wales
articles.description:
Lawyers launch super-complaint after research shows officers frequently dismiss image-based abuse

Police forces are routinely failing to investigate complaints about the circulation of image-based abuse, previously known as “revenge pornography”, according to research that has triggered a super-complaint over the way such crimes are handled.

Lawyers have gathered evidence from 100 people who reported intimate images being shared online without their consent. Their research suggests that image-based abuse is still frequently dismissed or not recognised as criminal offending, despite being described by the former prime minister Keir Starmer as a national emergency.

Continue reading...

articles.title: UK house prices flatline as rising mortgage costs weigh on market
articles.description:
Average cost of home in September was £298,441, says Lloyds – about the same as year earlier and in August

  • Business live – latest updates

UK house prices flatlined in September, according to a leading index, as rising mortgage costs started to weigh on the market.

The average cost of a home was £298,441, roughly the same as it was a year earlier and in the previous month, according to the tracker from Lloyds previously known as the Halifax HPI.

Continue reading...

articles.title: Flydubai attack investigation widens as alleged hijacker’s training in New Zealand scrutinised
articles.description:
Hamam al-Hammami spent 175 days in New Zealand until May 2019, as Australian Jewish group calls for full investigation into his time in Melbourne

New Zealand authorities have launched their own investigation into the flydubai co-pilot who allegedly tried to hijack an Israel-bound plane, after police confirmed he underwent flight training there about a year after he abandoned a degree in Australia.

Disaster was narrowly averted on 30 September when passengers and crew intervened to stop the alleged attempt of the co-pilot, Hamam al-Hammami, 29, to take control of a flight to Tel Aviv with 182 people onboard.

Continue reading...

articles.title: Naval drone hits oil tanker off Russian resort city Sochi, triggering massive blaze
articles.description:
Russian officials said a Liberian-flagged tanker was attacked and a crew of 23 Indian nationals rescued

An oil tanker off Russia’s Black Sea coast was struck by a naval drone, triggering a huge fire and black smoke cloud that blanketed parts of the resort city of Sochi, Russia’s transport ministry has said.

The transport ministry said a Liberian-flagged tanker had been attacked and that “crude oil is burning openly in the waters of the Black Sea”.

Continue reading...

articles.title: Friends of Nolan Wells sue NFL Hall of Famer Terrell Owens for defamation
articles.description:
Owens sued over September Instagram post that suggested trio tampered with evidence in death of Mississippi teen

Three friends of Nolan Wells, a Mississippi teen who died after a July boating trip, have sued NFL Hall of Famer Terrell Owens for defamation.

On 26 September, Owens shared an Instagram video that suggested Wells’s friends Warren Hudson, Jax Pitalo and Morgan Seymour had deleted evidence from Wells’s phone after his death, which the three men denied in their lawsuit.

Continue reading...

articles.title: Ikea to pilot online buyback service for secondhand furniture
articles.description:
Service to be tested in Spain and Portugal this year, with a UK rollout if successful, as pre-loved markets boom

Ikea is to test an online version of its buy-back service where the retailer offers vouchers for unwanted secondhand furniture.

The service will be tested in Spain and Portugal before the end of December and will be launched in the UK if it proves successful. Ikea already offers buy-back in stores, including in the UK. The online version will extend it to a much wider audience, with Ikea predicting pre-owned goods are likely to grab 16% of the UK homewares market by next year

Continue reading...

articles.title: Israeli settlers beat press photographer as soldiers watch in West Bank
articles.description:
Jaafar Ashtiyeh was covering violence against olive farmers when settlers set upon him with the butts of their rifles

Armed Israeli settlers beat a photographer in the presence of Israeli soldiers, hospitalising him, as he covered worsening settler violence against olive farmers in the occupied West Bank.

Jaafar Ashtiyeh, a 58-year-old veteran photographer for Agence France-Presse in Palestine, was assaulted by a group of settlers, who beat him with the butts of their rifles, despite him being marked as press. He was assaulted in view of about a dozen armed Israeli soldiers.

Continue reading...

articles.title: Senior academics set out key questions Cambridge must answer over Jason Arday’s death
articles.description:
Letter from more than 40 signatories says university has backed away from promised thorough review of events before death

Senior Cambridge academics have criticised the university’s plans to investigate Prof Jason Arday’s death as inadequate, and said those responsible for “serious failures of leadership” should face consequences.

In a letter to Chris Smith, Cambridge’s chancellor, the academics said “it is not yet clear” how the proposed review will answer difficult questions about the university’s involvement in the events leading up to Arday’s death, including its handling of the criticism Arday suffered after his appointment as professor of sociology of education in 2023.

Continue reading...

articles.title: California couple charged with child abuse in surrogacy scheme involving at least 21 kids
articles.description:
Silvia Zhang and Guojun Xuan had 15 children, aged between two months to 13 years, removed from their home

A California couple has been arrested on child abuse charges following an investigation into a surrogacy scheme involving at least 21 kids, police said on Tuesday.

Silvia Zhang and her husband, Guojun Xuan are expected to face conspiracy to commit child abuse charges, according to the Los Angeles county sheriff’s department.

Continue reading...

articles.title: British man arrested over suspected RAF Fairford terrorism plot
articles.description:
Counter-terrorism police say 22-year-old detained in London on suspicion of terrorism offences

A seventh man has been arrested in London on suspicion of terrorism offences as part of the investigation related to threats to RAF Fairford, police have said.

The 22-year-old British national was arrested in Westminster, central London, on suspicion of preparation of terrorist acts under section 5 of the Terrorism Act 2006, counter-terrorism police said.

Continue reading...

articles.title: Lawyer for one of Cornell 7 calls for special prosecutor to be removed over previous comments
articles.description: New York Attorney General Letitia James is investigating the rape allegations, but the lawyer says comments she made on the case should disqualify her.

articles.title: Asos warns customer data may be compromised after ‘unauthorised’ app access
articles.description:
Shares in fashion company fall nearly 10% after its app systems are accessed by ‘unidentified third party’

Asos is investigating unauthorised access to its app system after shoppers received a notification claiming hackers had “fully compromised” its data.

The online fashion retailer said basic personal information including name and contact details might have been accessed by an unidentified third party but it did not believe payment card records or passwords had been compromised.

Continue reading...

articles.title: Jailed Lego collector’s insurance scam highlights UK’s £1.3bn fraud problem
articles.description:
Industry leaders say bogus claims rose 14% last year, pushing up premiums for all customers

An insurance fraudster who pocketed more than £14,000 for the supposed theft of Lego sets, fishing gear and gaming consoles was behind one of last year’s most high-profile bogus claims.

Investigators uncovered £1.34bn of fraud in 2025, a 14% increase on the year before, according to the Association of British Insurers (ABI).

Continue reading...

articles.title: Veteran conservative lawyer quits Trump’s interior department and warns of ‘assault on the rule of law’
articles.description:
John Murdock had been working for the agency for 18 years and his resignation comes during an exodus of longtime federal workers and scientists

An 18-year veteran of the US Department of Interior has resigned in protest from the sprawling federal agency, denouncing “a deeply troubling assault on the rule of the law” that took place at the department under Donald Trump.

John Murdock, an attorney and self-described conservative Christian, began working for the agency’s legal office in 2002. In his resignation letter, first sent to his supervisor earlier this year and obtained exclusively by the Guardian and Public Domain, Murdock cites “glaring legal flaws” he witnessed within the agency during the course of the Trump administration, as well as concerns over offshore oil and gas drilling, the aggressive push to expand fossil fuels and the flouting of environmental regulation.

articles.title: Asos customers receive ‘hack’ notification threatening to leak data
articles.description:
Push message claims fashion company’s data has been ‘fully compromised’, but website and app remain online

  • Business live – latest updates

Asos is investigating after users of its mobile app received a notification claiming hackers had “fully compromised” the online fashion retailer’s data.

The value of Asos’s shares on the London Stock Exchange dived more than 14% after thousands of customers received a notification titled “Asos hacked” with a link that sent them to the Telegram messaging service.

Continue reading...

articles.title: Seven arrested for using Ghanaian banknotes to make 'money bouquets'
articles.description: The arrests are part of the country's efforts to curb the misuse and abuse of the national currency.

articles.title: Woman’s body found in stockyard trough close to NSW-Queensland border
articles.description:
Police say body found by trail bike riders at remote farm in Terragon is badly decomposed, sparking search of missing persons records

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

A partially submerged body believed to be a woman has been discovered in a remote stockyard, with the death being treated as suspicious.

Officers were called to a property in Terragon, near Murwillumbah in northern NSW, at about 11.20am on Monday after reports of a dead body.

Continue reading...

articles.title: Australian consumer confidence plunges to worst level since 1990s after RBA rate rise
articles.description:
Key indicator dropped about 20% after the Reserve Bank last month announced the highest interest rates since 2011

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

Australian households are the most persistently pessimistic they have been since the early-1990s recession, after a fourth rate rise this year.

Confidence among Australian consumers has plunged about 20% since the Reserve Bank of Australia lifted interest rates to the highest levels since 2011, according to the Westpac–Melbourne Institute consumer sentiment index.

articles.title: UK regulator FCA to investigate how it handled Epstein whistleblower who took his own life
articles.description:
British banker Simon Andriesz helped to expose alleged ties between late sex offender Jeffrey Epstein and US commerce secretary Howard Lutnick

A top UK regulator has launched an investigation into how it handled a whistleblower – who highlighted alleged ties between the late sex offender Jeffrey Epstein and the US commerce secretary, Howard Lutnick – after he took his own life.

The British banker Simon Andriesz died late last month aged 57, the campaign group Transparency Task Force, of which he was a member, confirmed over the weekend.

Continue reading...

articles.title: ‘I felt violated’: witness alleges Alan Jones kissed him and put hand on his bottom when he was 17
articles.description:
Radio host gave financial help to teenager after starting correspondence with him at the age of 13, court hears

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

When Alan Jones allegedly put his tongue inside the mouth of a 17-year-old and touched him on the bottom the teenager recoiled and withdrew to his ensuite where he scrubbed his mouth with a loofah, a Sydney court has heard.

“I felt violated and I felt gross,” the witness, who began corresponding with the broadcaster as a 13-year-old, said in his first day in the witness box where he is the fifth and final complainant in the lengthy trial of the former radio broadcaster.

articles.title: Fuel from South Korea being shipped to Russia as Ukraine war grinds on
articles.description:
Exclusive: Guardian analysis finds more than 150,000 tonnes of fuel was shipped to Russian ports in July and August, some using sanctioned tankers

Fuel is being shipped from South Korea to Russia via sanctioned tankers as Moscow scrambles for supplies amid the war in Ukraine, a move one expert said “undermines” Seoul’s public backing for Kyiv.

Guardian analysis of port records and ship-tracking data found that in July and August over 176,000 tonnes of fuel, mostly diesel, was loaded at several South Korean ports on to seven tankers that made 14 voyages to Russia’s far east.

Continue reading...

articles.description: The world's fastest growing major economy has one of the worst performing major equity markets in 2026.

articles.title: France braces for national day of school protests after injuries and mass arrests
articles.description: France prepares for a day of protests in support of students who’ve been demanding more investment in education.
